objective: Independent security review of PR7's removal of the record and local-file read caps and output cuts.
acceptance_criteria: Assesses what an attacker who controls committed .holyclaude records (a hostile or compromised repository) or local files can now do with unbounded reads (memory, time, hook timeouts, guard fail-open or fail-closed behavior), and whether the guard's PreToolUse path reads any now-unbounded file.
Assesses the removed deny-reason and CLI error cuts for output-injection or flooding risk.
Each finding traced source to sink with severity and fix, or none.
result: PR7 security review: no critical/high; medium F1 PreToolUse observe reads an unbounded repo-suppliable observations log on every subagent call (timeout or OOM fails the guard open); medium F2 quadratic validateState reachable via uncapped records/local files hangs SessionStart and CLI; low F3 uncapped committed records cost memory; low F4 legacy migration loads unbounded logs under the lock; low F5 removed output cuts mostly fine, CLI error may echo hostile record text. Fixes proposed that bound only untrusted reads or fix algorithms.

acceptance.rationale: Traced sources to sinks across observe, readGeneration, validateState, legacy migration; limits of reading stated.
